# FibreFlow Session Memory

## User
- [user_hein_profile.md](user_hein_profile.md) — Hein: Director/CTO, concise working style, visual verification, weekend infrastructure work
- Login credentials: see `.claude/credentials.local.md` (gitignored)

## Feedback
- [feedback_data_safety.md](feedback_data_safety.md) — Never lose work, never create duplicates, verify visually before confirming
- [feedback_qa_standards.md](feedback_qa_standards.md) — Never auto-approve incomplete QA, all required photos must be present
- [feedback_meeting_accuracy.md](feedback_meeting_accuracy.md) — Board minutes: zero hallucination, Gemini 2.5 Pro for Afrikaans, multi-pass pipeline
- [feedback_timezone_sast.md](feedback_timezone_sast.md) — All times SAST (UTC+2), recurring timezone error
- [feedback_pr_workflow.md](feedback_pr_workflow.md) — ALL changes through PRs, never edit deploy dirs directly
- [feedback_no_firebase.md](feedback_no_firebase.md) — VF Storage (100.96.203.105:8091), never Firebase
- [feedback_module_nav.md](feedback_module_nav.md) — Multi-page modules MUST use ModuleNav horizontal nav bar
- [feedback_noc_knowledge.md](feedback_noc_knowledge.md) — NOC: persist screenshots to VF Storage, write fix log per module after every resolution

## Project
- [project_billing_cycle.md](project_billing_cycle.md) — Billing cycles: Sunday 22:00 to Sunday 22:00 SAST
- [autoresearch-session-2026-03-22.md](autoresearch-session-2026-03-22.md) — Tech debt: react-router-dom, TS errors, VLM accuracy (campaigns ran 2026-03-24)
- [conduit-actuals-mapping.md](conduit-actuals-mapping.md) — COS from Data tab, Revenue from FT_Revenue, 8-report financial structure, EAC formula
- [boq-integrated-procurement.md](boq-integrated-procurement.md) — Migration 195, BOQLinePicker, requisition-to-PO with boq_item_id
- [drops-business-logic.md](drops-business-logic.md) — PO contracted vs spare drops, percentage denominator
- [hitl-approval-tracking.md](hitl-approval-tracking.md) — HITL approval needs consistent user attribution

## Reference

- [wa-monitor-troubleshooting.md](wa-monitor-troubleshooting.md) — Bridge architecture, ACK resilience, group JIDs

## Feedback (additional)

---

## Remaining Technical Debt (from 2026-03-22 AutoResearch session)

12 PRs merged, 56 skills modernized. On 2026-03-24, parallel agent campaigns addressed API response standardization, SELECT * elimination, and HITL few-shot wiring. Remaining items:

- **react-router-dom removal** — needs dead code audit of `src/pages/` and `src/app/router/` first
- **TypeScript errors** (~4,238) — top files: incidentLearning.ts (52), onemap/upload.ts (45), neon/api/server.ts (44)
- **SELECT * cleanup** — campaigns ran 2026-03-24, check remaining count
- **VLM accuracy auto-research loops** — needs ground truth test sets for iterative prompt optimization
- **Empty catch blocks** (~778) — most are intentional (safeOperations.ts) or JSON.parse fallbacks

**How to apply:** The AutoResearch skill at `.claude/skills/auto-research/SKILL.md` has modes for each area.

---
name: BOQ-Integrated Procurement
description: Migration 195, BOQLinePicker, requisition-to-PO flow with boq_item_id, utilization API
type: project
---

## BOQ-Integrated Procurement (2026-02-25)

- **Migration 195** (`scripts/migrations/195_boq_requisition_link.sql`) — adds `boq_item_id` + `item_type` to `purchase_requisition_items` (applied to production)
- **Shared types**: `src/types/procurement/boq-utilization.types.ts` — import from here (NOT from the API route path `[projectId]` which breaks TS imports)
- **API**: `pages/api/projects/[projectId]/boq-utilization.ts` — `GET` returns `{ summary, lines, nonBoqItems }`
- **BOQLinePicker**: `src/modules/procurement/workflow/steps/BOQLinePicker.tsx` — portaled searchable dropdown; color-coded by outstanding qty
- **RequisitionItemsTable**: BOQ/ad-hoc toggle per row; `boqItemId`, `onSelectBOQ`, `onClearBOQ` props added; `FormItem.itemType` added
- **Step1Requirements**: fetches `/api/projects/${projectId}/boq-utilization` when project changes; passes `boqLines` to table
- **Requisition API** (`pages/api/procurement/requisitions/index.ts`): persists `boq_item_id` + `item_type` per item
- **convert-to-po**: propagates `boq_item_id` + `item.item_code` from PR item -> PO item
- **BOQUtilizationTable**: `src/components/procurement/boq/BOQUtilizationTable.tsx` — on project `boq` tab above BOQList

---
name: Conduit Actuals Data Source Mapping
description: COS actuals come from Data tab, Revenue actuals from FT_Revenue tab — critical for Conduit financial sync
type: project
---

## Conduit Financial Data Sources (decided 2026-03-24)

- **COS (Cost of Sales) actuals** → sourced from the **Data tab** in the Conduit spreadsheet
- **Revenue actuals** → sourced from the **FT_Revenue tab**
- Column indices are specific per tab and were corrected in commit 1f326b4b

**Why:** Previous implementation incorrectly pulled COS from FT_Revenue. The Data tab has the authoritative COS figures. This distinction is critical for accurate project profitability.
**How to apply:** When working on Conduit sync or financial reports, always verify which tab is the source. COS ≠ Revenue source.

## Financial Reports Structure (decided 2026-03-22)

8-report structure: Income Statement, Project Profitability, Revenue by Client, Cashflow Statement, Operational Expenses, COS Breakdown, Assets Register, OPEX vs CAPEX. Split into Financial + Operations tabs under Analytics Reports.

## EAC (Revised Forecast)

EAC tiles only show for projects with `status === "wip" || status === "scoping"` AND `ft_project_name` set.
Formula: EAC = Actual-to-date + Remaining forecast.

# Deployment Workflow — Two Environments (2026-03-11)

## RULE: Dev-only during business hours

| Time | Dev | Production |
|------|-----|------------|
| 08:00-17:00 SAST Mon-Fri | Allowed | BLOCKED |
| After hours + weekends | Allowed | Promote from dev |
| Emergency (any time) | Allowed | --force required |

> **Staging retired 2026-03-11.** `vf.fibreflow.app` redirects to `app.fibreflow.app`. Standalone services (wa-proxy :8092, pdf-tools :3007) still route through the old vf.fibreflow.app nginx block.

## Environments

| Env | URL | Port | Service | Dir |
|-----|-----|------|---------|-----|
| Dev | dev.fibreflow.app | 3005 | `fibreflow-dev.service` | `/home/velo/fibreflow-dev/` |
| Production | app.fibreflow.app | 3000 | `fibreflow-production.service` | `/home/velo/fibreflow-production/` |
| Local | localhost:3004 | 3004 | manual | working copy |

## Primary: deploy-local.sh (one command, handles everything)

```bash
bash scripts/deploy-local.sh dev              # Deploy to dev (always)
bash scripts/deploy-local.sh production       # After hours only
bash scripts/deploy-local.sh status           # Show all environments
bash scripts/deploy-local.sh production --force  # Emergency override
```

**What it handles automatically:**
- Ownership fix (`sudo chown -R velo:velo`) — prevents EACCES from mixed hein/velo/root builds

**Pre-push** (`.git/hooks/pre-push`):
- GUARD 1: Allows Claude Code sessions (checks `CLAUDECODE=1` env var)

description: Every NOC ticket resolution must persist screenshots to VF Storage and write a fix log entry per module
type: feedback
---

Two mandatory post-resolution steps for every NOC ticket:

1. **Screenshots → VF Storage**: Use `node scripts/noc-attach-screenshot.js` immediately after every browser screenshot. NEVER leave proof-of-fix only in `/tmp/`. NEVER create `maintenance_attachments` records via direct SQL INSERT.

2. **Fix log entry**: Append structured entry to `.claude/knowledge-base/noc-fix-log/<module>.md` documenting root cause, fix, pattern, and lesson learned. This builds institutional knowledge per module so similar issues are diagnosed faster.

**Why:** On 2026-03-13 the NOC agent took screenshots but never uploaded them to VF Storage — proof-of-resolution was lost. Hein requires persistent evidence that tickets were actually resolved, and accumulated knowledge about what breaks per module.

**How to apply:** After every NOC ticket resolution: (1) upload screenshots via `noc-attach-screenshot.js`, (2) write fix log entry. Read existing fix log entries before diagnosing — the answer may already be there.

name: No Firebase — NEVER
description: FibreFlow does NOT use Firebase. Storage is VF Storage (self-hosted, 100.96.203.105:8091). NEVER assume or mention Firebase.
type: feedback
---

**FibreFlow does NOT use Firebase. Period.**

Storage is **VF Storage** — self-hosted on `100.96.203.105:8091`, served publicly via `https://vf.fibreflow.app/storage/`. Adapter: `src/services/vfStorageAdapter.ts`.

Upload directly: `curl -X POST http://100.96.203.105:8091/upload/{type}/{category} -F file=@path`

**Why:** User was extremely frustrated ("FFFFSSSSSSSS") when I assumed Firebase. CLAUDE.md itself had the wrong reference (now fixed). This is a hard rule — never guess storage backends, always check the code.

**How to apply:** Never mention Firebase in any FibreFlow context. When uploading files programmatically, use VF Storage directly (port 8091) or via the `/api/storage/upload` API. URLs follow pattern: `https://vf.fibreflow.app/storage/{type}/{category}/{filename}`.

## Key Learnings (2026-02-24 incident)

1. **Never use nginx upstream blocks with unreachable backup servers** — they cause stuck "no live upstreams" state
2. **Never use `fuser -k` in ExecStartPre** — it can kill unrelated processes on the same port
3. **Check for duplicate systemd services** when debugging port conflicts — `systemctl list-units | grep fibreflow`
4. **Git pre-commit hooks in deploy dirs** — block agent-named commits (Jarvis, Flow, Forge, etc.)
5. **Always verify .next ownership in ExecStartPre** — catches corrupted builds before crash-loop
6. **OpenClaw agents run as `hein`** — same user as the developer, so filesystem permissions alone aren't enough; git hooks provide the real enforcement

## Exec-Approvals (deployed 2026-02-23)

- **Config**: `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json`
- **Mode**: `allowlist` with `ask: on-miss`, `askFallback: deny`
- **72 safe binaries** allowlisted for all agents (git, curl, node, python, common unix tools)
- **Relay agent** locked to 11 read-only tools only (no git, no ssh, no npm, no docker)
- **Blocked by default**: rm, systemctl, kill, pkill, reboot, shutdown — anything not on the list

## Git Pre-Push Hook (deployed 2026-02-23, updated 2026-02-23)

- **Locations**: `.git/hooks/pre-push` in ALL 4 repos (local + 3 server)
  - `/home/hein/Workspace/FF_Next.js/.git/hooks/pre-push`

  - `/home/velo/fibreflow-staging/.git/hooks/pre-push`
  - `/home/velo/fibreflow-dev/.git/hooks/pre-push`
- **Guard 1 — Bot Master Protection** (whitelist approach):
  - Blocks ALL non-interactive pushes to `master`/`main` by default
  - Interactive human terminals pass through (tty check)
  - Override: `ALLOW_MASTER_PUSH=1 git push` (humans only)
  - Catches: OpenClaw agents, Jarvis (server Claude sessions), any automated process
- **Guard 2 — Auth Isolation Guard**: Scans for hardcoded userId patterns (dev-user-1, req.body.userId, etc.)
- **Agents must**: create feature branch → push → `gh pr create`
- **Lesson learned**: Original hook only checked `$OPENCLAW_AGENT` env var — Jarvis (server `git config user.name`) bypassed it because it's a direct Claude Code session, not an OpenClaw agent. Switched to whitelist: block everything non-interactive unless explicitly allowed.

# Procurement BOQ Import & Stock Matching (2026-02-12)

**File locations**: `src/services/procurement/import/materialMatcher.ts`, `stockMatcher.ts`, `fiberDomainMatcher.ts`

## BOQ Import Performance
**Problem**: Per-row DB queries (3+ per item × 250 rows = 750+ queries) cause Cloudflare ~100s proxy timeout.
**Solution**: Pre-load all materials once with `getAllMaterials()`, match in-memory with `matchItemWithCache()`.
- Made `getAllMaterials()` and `matchItemWithCache()` public in `materialMatcher.ts`
- Inlined BOQ item INSERT to skip redundant budget_categories SELECT per row
- Deferred match history recording to after main loop

## Stock Item Matching Pipeline
4-stage pipeline in `stockMatcher.ts`:
1. Supplier code lookup (exact match via supplier_item_codes table)
2. Exact/prefix item code match
3. Fiber domain match (category + parameter matching)
4. Fuzzy description + keyword overlap (threshold 0.55)

## Fiber Domain Matcher — Prefix Map
**Critical**: Stock item code prefixes MUST match actual stock data.
The initial prefix map used an older naming scheme that didn't exist in the database.

| BOQ Category | Actual Stock Prefix | Wrong Prefix |
|---|---|---|
| Drop Cable (Connectorised) | `DROP-APC-` | ~~`CAB-LCAPC-SCAPC-`~~ |
| Tangent (ADSS) | `TANGENT-` | ~~`CAB-TANGENT-`~~ |
| Dead-End(ADSS) | `DEADEND-` | ~~`CAB-DEADEND-`~~ |
| Enclosure (Connectorised) | `SJC-` | ~~`ENCL-CONN-`~~ |
| Enclosure (Splice) | `DOME-` | ~~`ENCL-SPLICE-`~~ |
| Splitter (Bare) | `SPLIT-BF-` | ~~`CAB-SPLITTER-BF-`~~ |
| Midcoupler | `MIDCOUP-` | ~~`CONS-MIDCOUPLER-`~~ |
| Splice Protector | `SPLICEPROTECTOR-` | ~~`CONS-SPLICEPROT-`~~ |

**Full mapping**: See `fiberDomainMatcher.ts` CATEGORY_PREFIX_MAP (~80 entries)

## BOQ Description Parsing Gotchas
- `G657A1.1:16` — the "1" before dot-separator can be corrupted by text-number separation regex
  - **Fix**: Only match 2+ digits before decimal: `([A-Za-z])(\d{2,}[.,]\d+)`
- `ADSS10.80-11.49mm` — text label stuck to number needs separation
- `13.6mm` vs stock `13.1mm` — need 0.6mm diameter tolerance (not 0.2mm)
- SLIMLINE variant in aerial cables is a label, not a real variant mismatch

## Stock Item Code Conventions (183 items, 7 categories)
| Category | Prefix Pattern | Example |
|----------|---------------|---------|
| activations | `DROP-APC-{len}-{dia}` | `DROP-APC-10-3` |
| stringing | `CAB-AER-SM-{dia}-{fiber}F` | `CAB-AER-SM-9.6-24F` |
| stringing | `TANGENT-{lo}-{hi}` | `TANGENT-10.80-11.49` |
| stringing | `DEADEND-{lo}-{hi}` | `DEADEND-9.2-9.5` |
| optics | `SJC-{model}` | `SJC-ODCFD0` |
| optics | `DOME-{model}` | `DOME-CMJ` |
| optics | `SPLIT-{type}-{ratio}` | `SPLIT-BF-1-8` |
| optics | `MIDCOUP-{type}-{conn}` | `MIDCOUP-D-LAPC-FL` |
| poles | `POLE-{height}-{range}` | `POLE-6-120-140` |

## Re-match API
`POST /api/procurement/boq/rematch-stock` — Re-runs stock matching without re-importing.
Preserves manual mappings (`stock_match_method = 'manual'`).

description: QField OES layer errors fixed 2026-03-24 — root cause was missing worker_wrapper storage config in docker-compose override
type: project

## Root Cause (FIXED 2026-03-24)
On March 21, `docker-compose.override.prod.yml` was replaced with a new version that **removed the `worker_wrapper` and `app` and `nginx` sections**. The workers lost their MinIO storage credentials, so `process_projectfile` couldn't read gpkg files to enrich layer metadata, and `package` couldn't include gpkg files in the download package.

**Fix:** Restored the `worker_wrapper`, `app`, and `nginx` sections to `/opt/qfieldcloud/docker-compose.override.prod.yml` and restarted workers.

**Why:** Without `STORAGE_ENDPOINT_URL`, `STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, etc., workers can't access MinIO where gpkg files are stored.

## Additional Issue: QGIS Docker Image Disappearing
The QGIS Docker image keeps going missing (March 21, 23, 24) and gets rebuilt from source each time. The backup tar.gz at `/home/velo/qfield-backups/` was deleted during storage migration. New image is QGIS 3.44.3 (was ~3.40 before). **Need to save current image as backup.**

## How `process_projectfile` Works
- Workers download ALL project files from MinIO
- QGIS opens the .qgs and validates all layers
- Minimal maplayer entries (5 children) get enriched to full entries (51 children) with SRS, extent, customproperties etc.
- The enriched .qgs is uploaded back and the version attr changes to current QGIS version
- **If workers can't access MinIO → layers don't get enriched → package excludes them → QField shows errors**

## Key Files
- `/opt/qfieldcloud/docker-compose.override.prod.yml` — MUST contain `worker_wrapper` section with storage config
- `/opt/qfield-sync/sync_oes_db_to_qfield.py` — daily OES sync script (creates minimal maplayer entries, relies on process_projectfile to enrich)
- `/opt/qfield-sync/sync_server.py` — webhook server on port 8095

## DO NOT
- Edit .qgs files with Python ElementTree — it corrupts XML attributes QGIS needs
- Delete old gpkg files from QFieldCloud — historical layers reference them
- Remove/replace `docker-compose.override.prod.yml` without preserving worker_wrapper section

# QField Photo Pipeline (updated 2026-03-25)

## Architecture
```
QField device → QFieldCloud → MinIO (qfieldcloud-prod)
                                ↓
                    extract-gpkg-photos.py (cron every 3h)
                                ↓
                    qfield_photo_validations table
                                ↓
                    /api/construction-qa/ingest-qfield
                                ↓
                    construction_qa_reviews + construction_qa_photos
                                ↓
                    VLM classification (Qwen3 on :8100)
                                ↓
                    Auto-approval (7+ photos, all steps covered)
```

## MinIO Access
- **Container**: `qfieldcloud-minio-1`
- **Bucket**: `qfieldcloud-prod`
- **Credentials**: `minioadmin/minioadmin` (from QFieldCloud app env)
- **mc alias**: `local` → `http://localhost:9000`

### CRITICAL: mc alias loses credentials on container restart
```bash
# Fix after restart:
docker exec qfieldcloud-minio-1 mc alias set local http://localhost:9000 minioadmin minioadmin
# Verify:
docker exec qfieldcloud-minio-1 mc ls local/qfieldcloud-prod/
```

### mc ls parsing: filenames can contain spaces
`mc ls` output has filenames like `civil-audit_20260309140815592.13.27 PM (1).jpeg` — DO NOT split on whitespace. Parse from `STANDARD` marker and use regex for version segment:
```python
std_idx = line.find(" STANDARD ")
rel_path = line[std_idx + len(" STANDARD "):].rstrip("/")
ver_match = re.search(r'/v(\d{14}-[a-fA-F0-9]+)$', rel_path)
```

### mc ls listing lag
Recently uploaded files may not appear in `mc ls --recursive` immediately, even though they exist by direct path. QFieldCloud DB (`filestorage_fileversion`) is authoritative.

## GPKG Extraction (`scripts/extract-gpkg-photos.py`)
- Downloads GPKG from MinIO, reads photo references from step columns
- Upserts into `qfield_photo_validations` with checklist_step
- Delta check: skips if GPKG version unchanged (use `--force` to override)
- Resolves photo filenames to versioned MinIO storage keys
- Photos referenced in GPKG but not yet in MinIO = "pending upload" (device sync lag)

### GPKG → device sync lag
The GPKG gets updated with photo references BEFORE the actual image files upload to MinIO. A pole can appear in the GPKG with 7 photos but have 0 files in MinIO. This is a device/connectivity issue, not server-side. The next extraction run picks them up once they sync.

---
name: SSH Access from Dell Laptop
description: How to SSH from the Dell laptop to Velocity server and VPS — keys, Tailscale IPs, config
type: reference
---

## SSH from Dell Laptop to Velocity Server

### Quick Connect
```bash
ssh hein@100.96.203.105
```

### Tailscale hostname (if MagicDNS enabled)
```bash
ssh hein@velo-server
```

### Recommended SSH config on Dell (`~/.ssh/config`)
```
Host velocity
    HostName 100.96.203.105
    User hein
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519

Host vps
    HostName 72.61.197.178
    User root
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```
Then: `ssh velocity` or `ssh vps`

### Server Details
| Server | Tailscale IP | Public IP | User |
|--------|-------------|-----------|------|
| Velocity | 100.96.203.105 | 192.168.1.150 (LAN) | hein |
| VPS | 100.100.65.113 | 72.61.197.178 | root |

### Auth
- Key-only (password auth disabled)
- Dell key (`hein@Hein-Dell` ed25519) is in `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` on Velocity
- Root login disabled on Velocity

### Troubleshooting
1. Check Tailscale running on Dell: `tailscale status`
2. Check key exists on Dell: `ls ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`
3. Test: `ssh hein@100.96.203.105 "echo OK"`

# STT — Handy Setup (2026-02-18)

## Setup
- **App**: Handy v0.7.6 (`/usr/bin/handy`, installed via .deb)
- **Model**: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2 (auto-downloaded, ~9s load)
- **Data**: `~/.local/share/com.pais.handy/`
- **Trigger**: Right Ctrl on Dell wireless keyboard (push-to-talk)

## Hotkey Listener
- **Script**: `~/.local/bin/handy-hotkey` (Python evdev)
- **Service**: `handy-hotkey.service` (systemd user, auto-start)
- **Device**: LITEON Dell Wireless Device (`04ca:00bd`), `/dev/input/event3`
- **Key**: `KEY_RIGHTCTRL` — hold to record, release to transcribe

## keyd Exclusion
Dell keyboard excluded from keyd in `/etc/keyd/default.conf`:
```
[ids]
  *
  -04ca:00bd
```
This allows direct evdev reads. keyd still handles Input Leap keyboard.

## Input Leap Context
- MacBook keyboard + mouse shared via Input Leap (`input-leapc`)
- XTest injection bypasses ALL X11 hotkey capture (xinput, xev, XRecord, pynput, Keybinder, GNOME extensions)
- Physical Dell keyboard is the ONLY way to capture hotkeys on this machine
- IBus trigger changed to Super+Space (was Ctrl+Space)

## CLI Toggle (works from any shell with correct env)
```bash
DISPLAY=:1 XAUTHORITY=/run/user/1003/gdm/Xauthority \
DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1003/bus \
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1003 GDK_BACKEND=x11 \
handy --toggle-transcription
```

## What DOESN'T Work (don't retry)
- Talon Voice (no speech model, needs Patreon)
- Nerd Dictation + Vosk (poor accuracy)
- evdev on keyd virtual keyboard (can't read from it)
- xinput/xev/XRecord/pynput/Keybinder (Input Leap XTest bypasses all)
- GNOME custom shortcuts (don't fire from XTest events)
- GNOME Shell extension key-press-event (only fires in overview)
- Scroll Lock as hotkey (breaks X11 modifier state)

name: WA Monitor Troubleshooting
description: WhatsApp bridge architecture, ACK resilience, duplicate ACK debugging, group JIDs, manual ACK commands
type: reference
---

## Bridge Architecture — Direct-Send (2026-02-18)
- **Sender service permanently disabled** — ACKs sent directly via bridge's own whatsmeow client
- `sender_proxy.go` uses `bridgeClient.SendMessage()` — no HTTP call, no external service
- Source code: `/home/velo/whatsapp-bridge/` (moved from `/home/louis/whatsapp-bridge-go/`)
- Old archives: `/home/velo/wa-bridge-build.archived/`, `/home/velo/whatsapp-bridge.old.20260114/`

## Bridge Binary Management (VPS)
- 20+ backup binaries in `/opt/whatsapp-bridge/`
- Current production: direct-send build (deployed 2026-02-18)
- Naming: `whatsapp-bridge.bak.YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_description`
- Latest backup: `whatsapp-bridge.bak.*_pre_direct_send`

## WA Sender Service — REMOVED (2026-02-18)
- **Permanently disabled and removed** from systemd on 2026-02-18
- Service file renamed to `whatsapp-sender.service.removed`
- No longer needed — bridge sends ACKs directly through its own WhatsApp client
- This eliminates WebSocket session conflicts (sender + bridge shared same phone session)

## Duplicate ACK Messages — OpenClaw Relay (2026-02-17)
**Problem**: Technicians receiving TWO ack messages per DR submission:
1. Bridge sends detailed ACK via `dr-acknowledgment.ts` (correct, immediate)
2. Gene (openclaw AI agent) sends short duplicate ACK ~5min later via bridge `/api/send`

**Root cause**: OpenClaw relay framework on Velocity (`~/.openclaw/relay/`) runs AI agents that monitor WA groups for unacked DRs and send messages directly to production WhatsApp groups.

**Key components** (DO NOT disable openclaw itself — user wants it running):
- `~/.openclaw/relay/workspace/scripts/dr-ack-watcher.py` — polls Neon + wacli SQLite every 90s
- Gene agent sends via `curl POST http://72.61.197.178:8083/api/send`
- Services: `openclaw-gene.service`, `openclaw-gateway.service`, etc. (systemd --user)

**If duplicate acks reappear**: Check openclaw agent sessions at `~/.openclaw/relay/agents/relay/sessions/` — grep for `8083/api/send` or `Received` to find which agent is sending.

## Manual ACK via Bridge (preferred over sender)
```bash
# 1. Get ACK message from FibreFlow API
curl -s -X POST "https://app.fibreflow.app/api/activate/dr-acknowledgment" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-bridge-secret: $WA_BRIDGE_SECRET" \
  -d '{"dropNumber": "DR123456"}'

# 2. Send via bridge (port 8083, stable connection)
curl -s http://72.61.197.178:8083/send-message -X POST \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"group_jid":"GROUP_JID","mention_jid":"SENDER_LID","message":"..."}'
```
**Note**: Bridge secret is in `.env.local` as `WA_BRIDGE_SECRET` (NOT `fibreflow-bridge-2026`)

## ACK Resilience Architecture (2026-03-09)
Bridge has 2-layer fallback — ACKs work even when FibreFlow is completely down:
- **Layer 1**: Multi-URL fallback: production -> dev -> staging (2 attempts each)
- **Layer 2**: Local ACK via direct Neon DB + BOSS API (Velocity:8003) — `ack_local.go`
- Source: `/home/velo/whatsapp-bridge/ack_local.go` + modified `sendDRAcknowledgment()` in `main.go`
- Backup binary: `/opt/whatsapp-bridge/whatsapp-bridge.bak.20260309_pre_local_ack`
- Log patterns: `[ACK FALLBACK]` = Layer 2, `[LOCAL ACK]` = local generation, `📱 ACK via FibreFlow API` = normal

## Error Code 1033 = Neon Database Timeout
Bridge logs: `[ACK WARN] Acknowledgment API returned 530 for DR123456: error code: 1033`
- Transient Neon timeout; usually self-resolves; bridge auto-retries across 3 URLs then falls back to local

## Data Source
Table: `pon_stage_tracking` joined to `projects`

Mapping:
- RFO (Ready for Optical) = cwc_complete / cwc_total (Civil Work Complete)
- ATP = atp_passed / atp_total (ATP QA passed)

SQL:
```sql
SELECT
  p.project_name,
  p.id as project_id,
  SUM(pst.cwc_total)     AS rfo_total,
  SUM(pst.cwc_complete)  AS rfo_complete,
  SUM(pst.atp_total)     AS atp_total,
  SUM(pst.atp_passed)    AS atp_passed
FROM pon_stage_tracking pst
JOIN projects p ON p.id = pst.project_id
WHERE p.status = 'active'
GROUP BY p.id, p.project_name
ORDER BY p.project_name
```

## Photo Upload Status Tracking

### The Dual-Sync Gap
QFieldCloud has two separate sync mechanisms:
1. **Delta push** (GPKG metadata) — syncs reliably within minutes
2. **File push** (DCIM photo binaries) — often lags or fails on poor connectivity

This means photo references exist in the GPKG before the actual files reach MinIO.

### upload_status Column (migration 243)
`construction_qa_photos.upload_status` tracks file availability:

| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `available` | File confirmed in MinIO (versioned path exists) |
| `pending_upload` | Ingested from GPKG but file not yet in MinIO |
| `missing` | Pending > 7 days, still not found |

### Photo Ingestion Flow
`scripts/extract-gpkg-photos.py` now:
1. Batch-lists the MinIO DCIM directory once per project
2. Only creates DB records for photos that have versioned files in MinIO
3. Skips photos not yet uploaded — they'll be picked up on the next run when the file appears

### Classify Cron Filter
`scripts/classify-qa-photos-vlm.py` skips `pending_upload` and `missing` photos — no wasted VLM calls on undownloadable files.

```bash

# Dry run
```

- Checks MinIO for each pending photo's versioned path

# /noc — NOC Tickets

Autonomous agent that picks up tickets from the NOC queue, triages by priority/SLA, diagnoses issues using the codebase, logs, and existing skills, implements fixes via PR workflow, deploys, verifies with screenshots, and resolves tickets with proof attached.

## Quick Reference

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| **Ticket table** | `maintenance_tickets` (type = `dev_ops`) |
| **Extension table** | `dev_ticket_details` (error_url, stack_trace, affected_module, etc.) |
| **Ticket UID format** | `VF-YYYYMMDD-NNN` |
| **API — list tickets** | `GET /api/noc/tickets?ticket_type=dev_ops&status=open,assigned` |
| **API — ticket detail** | `GET /api/noc/tickets/[id]` |
| **API — update ticket** | `PUT /api/noc/tickets/[id]` |
| **API — verification steps** | `GET/PUT /api/noc/tickets/[id]/verification/[step]` |
| **API — VLM screenshot** | `POST /api/noc/devops-vlm-analyse` |
| **Dev URL** | `https://dev.fibreflow.app` (port 3005) |
| **Prod URL** | `https://app.fibreflow.app` (port 3000) |
| **Local URL** | `http://localhost:3004` |

## Agent Workflow

When triggered, follow this sequence:

### Phase 1: Ticket Intake

```bash
# 1. Fetch open/assigned DevOps tickets
curl -s "http://localhost:3004/api/noc/tickets?ticket_type=dev_ops&status=open,assigned&limit=20" \
  -H "Cookie: $(cat .claude/credentials.local.md | grep SESSION | cut -d'=' -f2)" | jq '.data'
```

Or query the database directly:

```sql
-- Open DevOps tickets with details
SELECT
  t.id, t.ticket_uid, t.title, t.status, t.priority,
  t.created_at, t.assigned_to,
  d.affected_module, d.environment, d.error_url,
  d.stack_trace, d.steps_to_reproduce, d.browser_info,
  d.agent_status
FROM maintenance_tickets t
LEFT JOIN dev_ticket_details d ON d.ticket_id = t.id
WHERE t.ticket_type = 'dev_ops'
  AND t.status IN ('open', 'assigned', 'in_progress')
ORDER BY
  CASE t.priority
    WHEN 'critical' THEN 1
    WHEN 'urgent' THEN 2
    WHEN 'high' THEN 3
    WHEN 'normal' THEN 4
    WHEN 'low' THEN 5
  END,
  t.created_at ASC;
```

### Phase 2: Triage & Prioritize

For each ticket, assess:

1. **Severity** — Is production affected? How many users impacted?
2. **Module** — Which FibreFlow module? (Dashboard, NOC, Activate, Procurement, etc.)
3. **Reproducibility** — Can we reproduce from steps_to_reproduce?
4. **Quick win?** — Is it a known pattern (see Common Patterns below)?

**Priority matrix:**
| Priority | SLA | Action |
|----------|-----|--------|
| Critical | 6h | Drop everything, fix immediately |
| Urgent | 12h | Fix within session |
| High | 1d | Fix today |
| Normal | 3d | Queue for next session |
| Low | 7d | Backlog |

### Phase 3: Diagnosis

**Step 1 — Locate the affected code:**

```bash
# Find the module's source files
ls src/modules/<affected_module>/

# Find the API route if error_url points to an API
# Example: error on /api/noc/tickets → pages/api/noc/tickets.ts
find pages/api/ -name "*.ts" | grep <keyword>

# Find the page component if error_url points to a UI page
# Example: error on /projects/123 → pages/projects/[id]/index.tsx
find pages/ -name "*.tsx" | grep <keyword>
```

**Step 2 — Reproduce the error:**

Use the `steps_to_reproduce` from the ticket. If it's a UI issue, use browser automation:

```
1. mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp  (get browser context)
2. mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate          (go to error_url)
3. mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page         (get page state)
4. mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer          (follow reproduction steps)
```

**Step 3 — Analyze the stack trace:**

If `stack_trace` is provided, trace it through the codebase:

```bash
# Search for the error message in code
rg "ErrorMessage" src/ pages/

# Check the specific file:line from stack trace
# Read the file at that location
```

**Step 4 — Check logs:**

```bash
# Dev server logs
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-dev.service --since "1 hour ago" | grep -i error

# Production logs
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "1 hour ago" | grep -i error

# Check for specific error patterns
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-dev.service --since "1 hour ago" | grep "<ticket_keyword>"
```

**Step 5 — Database investigation:**

```sql
-- Check for data issues related to the ticket
-- Example: missing records, null values, constraint violations
SELECT * FROM <related_table> WHERE <condition> LIMIT 10;
```

### Phase 4: Fix Implementation

**Follow the PR workflow (MANDATORY):**

1. Create a feature branch: `fix/noc-<ticket_uid>-<short-description>`
2. Implement the fix
3. Run quality checks: `npm run lint && npm run type-check`
4. Run tests: `npm test`
5. Create PR via `/pr` skill
6. Update the ticket with PR link

**Update ticket status as you work:**

```sql
-- Mark ticket as in_progress when starting work
UPDATE maintenance_tickets SET status = 'in_progress' WHERE id = '<ticket_id>';

-- Update dev_ticket_details with branch/PR
UPDATE dev_ticket_details
SET github_branch = 'fix/noc-VF-XXXXXXXX-XXX-description',
    github_pr_url = 'https://github.com/VelocityFibre/FF_Next.js/pull/XXX',
    agent_status = 'running'
WHERE ticket_id = '<ticket_id>';
```

### Phase 5: Verification

DevOps tickets have 5 verification steps:

| Step | Name | Photo Required | Description |
|------|------|----------------|-------------|
| 1 | Issue Reproduction | Yes | Screenshot of the reproduced error |
| 2 | Root Cause Analysis | No | Document the root cause in notes |
| 3 | Fix Implementation | No | Link the PR, describe the fix |
| 4 | Testing & Verification | Yes | Screenshot of fix working in dev |
| 5 | Deployment | Yes | Screenshot of fix working in prod |

```bash
# Update verification step (example: step 2 - root cause)
curl -X PUT "http://localhost:3004/api/noc/tickets/<id>/verification/2" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "completed": true,
    "notes": "Root cause: missing null check in X component causing crash when Y is undefined"
  }'
```

#### MANDATORY: Upload Screenshots as Ticket Attachments

**Every screenshot taken during ticket work MUST be uploaded as a ticket attachment.**
Screenshots that only exist in `/tmp/` are lost when the session ends. The attachment API persists them permanently.

**How to upload a screenshot to a ticket:**

```bash
# 1. Take screenshot using browser tools (saves to /tmp/screenshot-*.png)
# 2. Upload to ticket attachments API:
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

const TICKET_ID = '<ticket-id>';
const FILE_PATH = '/tmp/screenshot.png';
const USER_ID = '<user-uid>';  // Use Hein's uid from auth context
const IS_EVIDENCE = 'true';    // true for verification step screenshots

const FormData = require('form-data');  // Built into Node 18+
const form = new FormData();
form.append('file', fs.createReadStream(FILE_PATH));
form.append('uploaded_by', USER_ID);
form.append('is_evidence', IS_EVIDENCE);

fetch('http://localhost:3004/api/noc/tickets/' + TICKET_ID + '/attachments', {
  method: 'POST',
  body: form,
}).then(r => r.json()).then(j => console.log(JSON.stringify(j, null, 2)));
"
```

**Or use the helper script:**

```bash
# Upload screenshot to ticket attachments
node scripts/noc-attach-screenshot.js <ticket-id> <file-path> [--evidence]
```

**When to upload screenshots:**

| Phase | Screenshot | `is_evidence` |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Step 1: Issue Reproduction | Screenshot showing the bug | `true` |
| Step 4: Testing & Verification | Screenshot showing fix works on dev | `true` |
| Step 5: Deployment | Screenshot showing fix works on prod | `true` |
| Diagnosis (optional) | Console errors, network tab, etc. | `false` |

**After fix is deployed and verified**, upload the "after" screenshot showing the issue is resolved:
1. Navigate to the affected page in the browser
2. Take a screenshot
3. Upload it with `is_evidence=true`
4. This provides proof-of-fix that persists on the ticket permanently

## Common Patterns (Known Issues)

### Pattern: API returns `data.data` (double-wrapped response)
**Symptom:** UI shows blank/undefined values
**Cause:** `apiResponse.success(res, { success: true, data: {...} })` double-wraps
**Fix:** Remove inner wrapper — just pass the raw data to `apiResponse.success(res, data)`
**Ref:** Memory `MEMORY.md` — "apiResponse.success() Double-Wrapping Anti-Pattern"

### Pattern: Conditional SQL fragment breaks Neon
**Symptom:** SQL syntax error, query returns unexpected results
**Cause:** `${cond ? sql\`AND x\` : sql\`\`}` — template literal fragments don't compose in Neon
**Fix:** Use explicit query branches (if/else with full queries)
**Ref:** CLAUDE.md — "NO Conditional SQL Fragments"

### Pattern: Dynamic route params `undefined`
**Symptom:** API returns 404 or "invalid UUID"
**Cause:** Nested dynamic routes fail on Vercel, or inconsistent param names
**Fix:** Flatten routes (`contractors-stages.ts` not `[id]/stages.ts`), use consistent `[projectId]`

### Pattern: Numeric values are strings from Neon
**Symptom:** Math operations return NaN or concatenate instead of add
**Cause:** Neon returns numeric columns as strings
**Fix:** Always `Number()` before arithmetic

### Pattern: Missing `credentials: 'include'` in fetch
**Symptom:** 401 Unauthorized on API calls
**Cause:** Auth cookie not sent with request
**Fix:** Add `credentials: 'include'` to all fetch calls

### Pattern: `console.log` in production code
**Symptom:** Lint error or log noise
**Fix:** Replace with `import { log } from '@/lib/logger'` — use `log.info()`, `log.error()`, etc.

### Pattern: File > 300 lines
**Symptom:** Quality violation
**Fix:** Extract components/utilities into separate files

## Escalation Rules

Escalate (don't attempt to fix) when:

1. **Database schema change required** — Needs migration review + Hein approval
2. **Production data corruption** — Flag immediately, don't modify data
3. **Auth/security issue** — Credential leak, permission bypass → escalate to Hein
4. **Third-party API down** — Neon, QContact, 1Map, Sage → wait/retry, notify Hein
5. **Infrastructure issue** — Server/service down → use `/infra` skill or notify Hein
6. **Unclear reproduction** — Can't reproduce after 3 attempts → ask reporter for more detail

**Escalation template:**

## Lessons Learned (Updated per ticket)

### 2026-03-13: VF-20260313-133 + VF-20260313-134
- **Schema column names differ from TypeScript types**: DB uses `type` not `ticket_type`, `status` not `ticket_status`. Always check actual schema with `\d maintenance_tickets` before querying.
- **psql connection**: Local psql defaults to port 5434 via socket. Use explicit: `PGPASSWORD=<pw> psql -h <host> -p 5432 -U neondb_owner -d neondb --set=sslmode=require`
- **z-index patterns**: ALL modals in codebase use `z-50` (not design tokens). Design system defines `--ff-z-modal-backdrop: 1040` and `--ff-z-modal: 1050` but they were never adopted. When fixing z-index, note this is a codebase-wide pattern, not a single-modal bug.
- **maintenance_notes schema**: Uses `created_by` (not `author_id`), has `is_resolution` boolean flag, `note_type` must be one of: internal, external, system.
- **Chrome DevTools scrolling**: Page content is in a `<main>` element that scrolls independently. Use `document.querySelector('main').scrollTop += N` via `evaluate_script`.
- **PR merge**: Branch protection requires `--admin` flag for gh merge. Auto-merge not enabled on repo.
- **Deploy workflow**: `sudo -u velo bash -c 'cd /home/velo/fibreflow-dev && git pull origin master && npm run build'` then `sudo systemctl restart fibreflow-dev.service`.

# /noc — NOC Tickets

Autonomous agent that picks up tickets from the NOC queue, triages by priority/SLA, diagnoses issues using the codebase, logs, and existing skills, implements fixes via PR workflow, deploys, verifies with screenshots, and resolves tickets with proof attached.

## Quick Reference

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| **Ticket table** | `maintenance_tickets` (type = `dev_ops`) |
| **Extension table** | `dev_ticket_details` (error_url, stack_trace, affected_module, etc.) |
| **Ticket UID format** | `VF-YYYYMMDD-NNN` |
| **API — list tickets** | `GET /api/noc/tickets?ticket_type=dev_ops&status=open,assigned` |
| **API — ticket detail** | `GET /api/noc/tickets/[id]` |
| **API — update ticket** | `PUT /api/noc/tickets/[id]` |
| **API — verification steps** | `GET/PUT /api/noc/tickets/[id]/verification/[step]` |
| **API — VLM screenshot** | `POST /api/noc/devops-vlm-analyse` |
| **Dev URL** | `https://dev.fibreflow.app` (port 3005) |
| **Prod URL** | `https://app.fibreflow.app` (port 3000) |
| **Local URL** | `http://localhost:3004` |

## Agent Workflow

When triggered, follow this sequence:

### Phase 1: Ticket Intake

```bash
# 1. Fetch open/assigned DevOps tickets
curl -s "http://localhost:3004/api/noc/tickets?ticket_type=dev_ops&status=open,assigned&limit=20" \
  -H "Cookie: $(cat .claude/credentials.local.md | grep SESSION | cut -d'=' -f2)" | jq '.data'
```

Or query the database directly:

```sql
-- Open DevOps tickets with details
SELECT
  t.id, t.ticket_uid, t.title, t.status, t.priority,
  t.created_at, t.assigned_to,
  d.affected_module, d.environment, d.error_url,
  d.stack_trace, d.steps_to_reproduce, d.browser_info,
  d.agent_status
FROM maintenance_tickets t
LEFT JOIN dev_ticket_details d ON d.ticket_id = t.id
WHERE t.ticket_type = 'dev_ops'
  AND t.status IN ('open', 'assigned', 'in_progress')
ORDER BY
  CASE t.priority
    WHEN 'critical' THEN 1
    WHEN 'urgent' THEN 2
    WHEN 'high' THEN 3
    WHEN 'normal' THEN 4
    WHEN 'low' THEN 5
  END,
  t.created_at ASC;
```

### Phase 2: Triage & Prioritize

For each ticket, assess:

1. **Severity** — Is production affected? How many users impacted?
2. **Module** — Which FibreFlow module? (Dashboard, NOC, Activate, Procurement, etc.)
3. **Reproducibility** — Can we reproduce from steps_to_reproduce?
4. **Quick win?** — Is it a known pattern (see Common Patterns below)?

**Priority matrix:**
| Priority | SLA | Action |
|----------|-----|--------|
| Critical | 6h | Drop everything, fix immediately |
| Urgent | 12h | Fix within session |
| High | 1d | Fix today |
| Normal | 3d | Queue for next session |
| Low | 7d | Backlog |

### Phase 3: Diagnosis

**Step 1 — Locate the affected code:**

```bash
# Find the module's source files
ls src/modules/<affected_module>/

# Find the API route if error_url points to an API
# Example: error on /api/noc/tickets → pages/api/noc/tickets.ts
find pages/api/ -name "*.ts" | grep <keyword>

# Find the page component if error_url points to a UI page
# Example: error on /projects/123 → pages/projects/[id]/index.tsx
find pages/ -name "*.tsx" | grep <keyword>
```

**Step 2 — Reproduce the error:**

Use the `steps_to_reproduce` from the ticket. If it's a UI issue, use browser automation:

```
1. mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp  (get browser context)
2. mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate          (go to error_url)
3. mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page         (get page state)
4. mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer          (follow reproduction steps)
```

**Step 3 — Analyze the stack trace:**

If `stack_trace` is provided, trace it through the codebase:

```bash
# Search for the error message in code
rg "ErrorMessage" src/ pages/

# Check the specific file:line from stack trace
# Read the file at that location
```

**Step 4 — Check logs:**

```bash
# Dev server logs
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-dev.service --since "1 hour ago" | grep -i error

# Production logs
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "1 hour ago" | grep -i error

# Check for specific error patterns
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-dev.service --since "1 hour ago" | grep "<ticket_keyword>"
```

**Step 5 — Database investigation:**

```sql
-- Check for data issues related to the ticket
-- Example: missing records, null values, constraint violations
SELECT * FROM <related_table> WHERE <condition> LIMIT 10;
```

### Phase 4: Fix Implementation

**Follow the PR workflow (MANDATORY):**

1. Create a feature branch: `fix/noc-<ticket_uid>-<short-description>`
2. Implement the fix
3. Run quality checks: `npm run lint && npm run type-check`
4. Run tests: `npm test`
5. Create PR via `/pr` skill
6. Update the ticket with PR link

**Update ticket status as you work:**

```sql
-- Mark ticket as in_progress when starting work
UPDATE maintenance_tickets SET status = 'in_progress' WHERE id = '<ticket_id>';

-- Update dev_ticket_details with branch/PR
UPDATE dev_ticket_details
SET github_branch = 'fix/noc-VF-XXXXXXXX-XXX-description',
    github_pr_url = 'https://github.com/VelocityFibre/FF_Next.js/pull/XXX',
    agent_status = 'running'
WHERE ticket_id = '<ticket_id>';
```

### Phase 5: Verification

DevOps tickets have 5 verification steps:

| Step | Name | Photo Required | Description |
|------|------|----------------|-------------|
| 1 | Issue Reproduction | Yes | Screenshot of the reproduced error |
| 2 | Root Cause Analysis | No | Document the root cause in notes |
| 3 | Fix Implementation | No | Link the PR, describe the fix |
| 4 | Testing & Verification | Yes | Screenshot of fix working in dev |
| 5 | Deployment | Yes | Screenshot of fix working in prod |

```bash
# Update verification step (example: step 2 - root cause)
curl -X PUT "http://localhost:3004/api/noc/tickets/<id>/verification/2" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "completed": true,
    "notes": "Root cause: missing null check in X component causing crash when Y is undefined"
  }'
```

#### MANDATORY: Upload Screenshots as Ticket Attachments

**Every screenshot taken during ticket work MUST be uploaded as a ticket attachment.**
Screenshots that only exist in `/tmp/` are lost when the session ends. The attachment API persists them permanently.

**How to upload a screenshot to a ticket:**

```bash
# 1. Take screenshot using browser tools (saves to /tmp/screenshot-*.png)
# 2. Upload to ticket attachments API:
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

const TICKET_ID = '<ticket-id>';
const FILE_PATH = '/tmp/screenshot.png';
const USER_ID = '<user-uid>';  // Use Hein's uid from auth context
const IS_EVIDENCE = 'true';    // true for verification step screenshots

const FormData = require('form-data');  // Built into Node 18+
const form = new FormData();
form.append('file', fs.createReadStream(FILE_PATH));
form.append('uploaded_by', USER_ID);
form.append('is_evidence', IS_EVIDENCE);

fetch('http://localhost:3004/api/noc/tickets/' + TICKET_ID + '/attachments', {
  method: 'POST',
  body: form,
}).then(r => r.json()).then(j => console.log(JSON.stringify(j, null, 2)));
"
```

**Or use the helper script:**

```bash
# Upload screenshot to ticket attachments
node scripts/noc-attach-screenshot.js <ticket-id> <file-path> [--evidence]
```

**When to upload screenshots:**

| Phase | Screenshot | `is_evidence` |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Step 1: Issue Reproduction | Screenshot showing the bug | `true` |
| Step 4: Testing & Verification | Screenshot showing fix works on dev | `true` |
| Step 5: Deployment | Screenshot showing fix works on prod | `true` |
| Diagnosis (optional) | Console errors, network tab, etc. | `false` |

**After fix is deployed and verified**, upload the "after" screenshot showing the issue is resolved:
1. Navigate to the affected page in the browser
2. Take a screenshot
3. Upload it with `is_evidence=true`
4. This provides proof-of-fix that persists on the ticket permanently

## Common Patterns (Known Issues)

### Pattern: API returns `data.data` (double-wrapped response)
**Symptom:** UI shows blank/undefined values
**Cause:** `apiResponse.success(res, { success: true, data: {...} })` double-wraps
**Fix:** Remove inner wrapper — just pass the raw data to `apiResponse.success(res, data)`
**Ref:** Memory `MEMORY.md` — "apiResponse.success() Double-Wrapping Anti-Pattern"

### Pattern: Conditional SQL fragment breaks Neon
**Symptom:** SQL syntax error, query returns unexpected results
**Cause:** `${cond ? sql\`AND x\` : sql\`\`}` — template literal fragments don't compose in Neon
**Fix:** Use explicit query branches (if/else with full queries)
**Ref:** CLAUDE.md — "NO Conditional SQL Fragments"

### Pattern: Dynamic route params `undefined`
**Symptom:** API returns 404 or "invalid UUID"
**Cause:** Nested dynamic routes fail on Vercel, or inconsistent param names
**Fix:** Flatten routes (`contractors-stages.ts` not `[id]/stages.ts`), use consistent `[projectId]`

### Pattern: Numeric values are strings from Neon
**Symptom:** Math operations return NaN or concatenate instead of add
**Cause:** Neon returns numeric columns as strings
**Fix:** Always `Number()` before arithmetic

### Pattern: Missing `credentials: 'include'` in fetch
**Symptom:** 401 Unauthorized on API calls
**Cause:** Auth cookie not sent with request
**Fix:** Add `credentials: 'include'` to all fetch calls

### Pattern: `console.log` in production code
**Symptom:** Lint error or log noise
**Fix:** Replace with `import { log } from '@/lib/logger'` — use `log.info()`, `log.error()`, etc.

### Pattern: File > 300 lines
**Symptom:** Quality violation
**Fix:** Extract components/utilities into separate files

### 2026-03-13: VF-20260313-133 + VF-20260313-134
- **Schema column names differ from TypeScript types**: DB uses `type` not `ticket_type`, `status` not `ticket_status`. Always check actual schema with `\d maintenance_tickets` before querying.
- **psql connection**: Local psql defaults to port 5434 via socket. Use explicit: `PGPASSWORD=<pw> psql -h <host> -p 5432 -U neondb_owner -d neondb --set=sslmode=require`
- **z-index patterns**: ALL modals in codebase use `z-50` (not design tokens). Design system defines `--ff-z-modal-backdrop: 1040` and `--ff-z-modal: 1050` but they were never adopted. When fixing z-index, note this is a codebase-wide pattern, not a single-modal bug.
- **maintenance_notes schema**: Uses `created_by` (not `author_id`), has `is_resolution` boolean flag, `note_type` must be one of: internal, external, system.
- **Chrome DevTools scrolling**: Page content is in a `<main>` element that scrolls independently. Use `document.querySelector('main').scrollTop += N` via `evaluate_script`.

# /kb - Knowledge Base Update

Update the FibreFlow knowledge base by scanning modules and refreshing context files.

## Usage

```
/kb              # Full scan and update
/kb status       # Show KB status only
/kb [module]     # Update specific module
```

## What This Does

1. **Scan Modules** - Find all `src/modules/*/` directories
2. **Check Coverage** - Identify modules missing `.claude.md`
3. **Generate Context** - Create `.claude.md` for missing modules
4. **Consolidate Learnings** - Move `.claude-learnings.md` entries to permanent KB
5. **Qdrant Ingestion** - Push all KB sources into Qdrant vector DB on Velocity
6. **Update Session** - Record KB update in session state

## Execution Steps

### Step 1: Scan Modules
```bash
# Count total modules
ls -d src/modules/*/ | wc -l

# List modules with .claude.md
find src/modules -maxdepth 2 -name ".claude.md" | wc -l

# List modules WITHOUT .claude.md
for dir in src/modules/*/; do
  name=$(basename "$dir")
  if [ ! -f "$dir/.claude.md" ]; then
    echo "❌ $name"
  fi
done
```

### Step 2: For Each Missing Module
Generate `.claude.md` using template from `.claude/templates/module-claude-md.template`:
- Extract purpose from README.md or code
- List key files (services, components, types)
- Identify API endpoints from `pages/api/`
- Note critical rules and common issues

### Step 3: Consolidate Learnings
Check for `.claude-learnings.md` files with entries >7 days old:
```bash
find src/modules -name ".claude-learnings.md" -exec echo "Found: {}" \;
```
Move old entries to module's `.claude.md` under "## Learnings" section.

### Step 4: Update Session State
Update `.claude/session/current.json`:
```json
{
  "last_action": "KB update via /kb",
  "kb_scan_results": {
    "timestamp": "...",
    "total_modules": N,
    "modules_with_claude_md": N
  }
}
```

### Step 5: Qdrant Vector DB Ingestion
Push all KB markdown sources + DB schema into the Qdrant vector database on Velocity.
This keeps the vector search in sync with local knowledge files.

```bash
# Full re-ingestion (recommended during /kb)
cd /home/velo/fibreflow-production && export $(grep DATABASE_URL .env) && scripts/.venv/bin/python scripts/ingest-qdrant.py --force 2>&1
```

The script:
- Scans `docs/*.md`, `.claude/modules/*.md`, `.claude/knowledge-base/**/*.md`, `src/modules/*/.claude.md`
- Chunks by `##` headings (~800 word chunks with paragraph overlap)
- Embeds with OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` (1536-dim)
- Upserts into Qdrant collection `fibreflow_kb` at `localhost:6333`
- Also ingests DB schema from `information_schema`
- Uses deterministic point IDs (source + chunk_index hash) so re-runs replace, not duplicate

Flags: `--force` (re-ingest all), `--source <path>` (single file), `--dry-run` (count only).

### Step 6: Report Results
```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                    KB UPDATE COMPLETE                        ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║ Modules scanned:        41                                   ║
║ With .claude.md:        41 (100%)                            ║
║ Learnings consolidated: 0                                    ║
║ Qdrant chunks ingested: 8761                                 ║
║ Qdrant collection:      fibreflow_kb (green)                 ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

## Related Files

|------|---------|
| `.claude/session/current.json` | Session state |
| `.claude/templates/module-claude-md.template` | Template |
| `src/modules/*/.claude.md` | Module context |
| `src/modules/*/.claude-learnings.md` | Auto-captured learnings |
| `scripts/ingest-qdrant.py` | Qdrant vector DB ingestion script |

## Task: Fix Conduit actuals sync — pull COS from Data tab, not FT_Revenue

### Problem
`app/api/conduit/actuals/sync/route.ts` currently pulls from FT_Revenue tab (Type=invoice rows) and stores the "Type" column as cos_breakdown keys — producing `Activations`, `Backaul`, `Fuel` as COS categories which is wrong.

### Correct approach
COS actuals must come from the **Data tab** (not FT_Revenue):
- Column indices (0-based): Date(0), Date_M(1), Type(3), Amount Excl VAT(5), Category T2(10), Cost Centre T2(15)
- Filter rows where: `Type === "Expense"` AND `Category T2` starts with `"COS"`
- Group by: Cost Centre T2 (= project name, matches ft_project_name) + month (from Date_M)
- Amount: sum of `Amount Excl VAT` (index 5) per project+month+category
- Exclude Cost Centre T2 values: "OPEX", "Revenue", "Loan", "Tools", "Fixed Assets", "None", "Liabilities"

Revenue actuals come from **FT_Revenue tab**:
- Column indices (0-based): Invoice Date(0), Date_M(1), Type(3), Project(7), Cost Type(8), Debit Excl VAT(9), Activations(13)
- Filter rows where: `Type === "invoice"`
- Revenue actual: sum of `Debit Excl VAT` (index 9) per project+month
- Activations: sum of Activations (index 13) per project+month

### Rewrite app/api/conduit/actuals/sync/route.ts

The rewritten route should:
1. Fetch both `Data` and `FT_Revenue` worksheets via `getWorksheetRange`
2. Process Data tab → cos_actual + cos_breakdown (keyed by Category T2, e.g. "COS - Fuel")
3. Process FT_Revenue tab → revenue_actual + activations
4. Merge by project+month
5. Upsert into conduit_actuals

Check the existing conduit_actuals table schema first:
```sql
SELECT column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = "conduit_actuals"
```
The table has: project_name, month, cos_actual, activations, cos_breakdown (jsonb), synced_at
Check if revenue_actual column exists — if not, add it:
`ALTER TABLE conduit_actuals ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS revenue_actual numeric DEFAULT 0`

### Cutoff rule
Only include months where monthFirst < first day of current month UTC.

### Date parsing
Date_M column in both tabs may be Excel serial numbers (number) or date strings.
Excel serial: `new Date(Date.UTC(1899, 11, 30) + serialNumber * 86400000)`

### Non-project Cost Centre T2 values to exclude
"OPEX", "Revenue", "Loan", "Tools", "Fixed Assets", "None", "Liabilities", ""

### After rewriting the route:
1. Run: `npx tsc --noEmit` — fix any type errors
2. Branch: `fix/conduit-actuals-sync-data-tab`
3. Commit: "fix(conduit): sync COS actuals from Data tab, revenue from FT_Revenue"
4. Push + open PR against master

# /noc — NOC Tickets

Autonomous agent that picks up tickets from the NOC queue, triages by priority/SLA, diagnoses issues using the codebase, logs, and existing skills, implements fixes via PR workflow, deploys, verifies with screenshots, and resolves tickets with proof attached.

## Quick Reference

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| **Ticket table** | `maintenance_tickets` (type = `dev_ops`) |
| **Extension table** | `dev_ticket_details` (error_url, stack_trace, affected_module, etc.) |
| **Ticket UID format** | `VF-YYYYMMDD-NNN` |
| **API — list tickets** | `GET /api/noc/tickets?ticket_type=dev_ops&status=open,assigned` |
| **API — ticket detail** | `GET /api/noc/tickets/[id]` |
| **API — update ticket** | `PUT /api/noc/tickets/[id]` |
| **API — verification steps** | `GET/PUT /api/noc/tickets/[id]/verification/[step]` |
| **API — VLM screenshot** | `POST /api/noc/devops-vlm-analyse` |
| **Dev URL** | `https://dev.fibreflow.app` (port 3005) |
| **Prod URL** | `https://app.fibreflow.app` (port 3000) |
| **Local URL** | `http://localhost:3004` |

## Agent Workflow

When triggered, follow this sequence:

### Phase 1: Ticket Intake

```bash
# 1. Fetch open/assigned DevOps tickets
curl -s "http://localhost:3004/api/noc/tickets?ticket_type=dev_ops&status=open,assigned&limit=20" \
  -H "Cookie: $(cat .claude/credentials.local.md | grep SESSION | cut -d'=' -f2)" | jq '.data'
```

Or query the database directly:

```sql
-- Open DevOps tickets with details
SELECT
  t.id, t.ticket_uid, t.title, t.status, t.priority,
  t.created_at, t.assigned_to,
  d.affected_module, d.environment, d.error_url,
  d.stack_trace, d.steps_to_reproduce, d.browser_info,
  d.agent_status
FROM maintenance_tickets t
LEFT JOIN dev_ticket_details d ON d.ticket_id = t.id
WHERE t.ticket_type = 'dev_ops'
  AND t.status IN ('open', 'assigned', 'in_progress')
ORDER BY
  CASE t.priority
    WHEN 'critical' THEN 1
    WHEN 'urgent' THEN 2
    WHEN 'high' THEN 3
    WHEN 'normal' THEN 4
    WHEN 'low' THEN 5
  END,
  t.created_at ASC;
```

### Phase 2: Triage & Prioritize

For each ticket, assess:

1. **Severity** — Is production affected? How many users impacted?
2. **Module** — Which FibreFlow module? (Dashboard, NOC, Activate, Procurement, etc.)
3. **Reproducibility** — Can we reproduce from steps_to_reproduce?
4. **Quick win?** — Is it a known pattern (see Common Patterns below)?

**Priority matrix:**
| Priority | SLA | Action |
|----------|-----|--------|
| Critical | 6h | Drop everything, fix immediately |
| Urgent | 12h | Fix within session |
| High | 1d | Fix today |
| Normal | 3d | Queue for next session |
| Low | 7d | Backlog |

### Phase 3: Diagnosis

**Step 1 — Locate the affected code:**

```bash
# Find the module's source files
ls src/modules/<affected_module>/

# Find the API route if error_url points to an API
# Example: error on /api/noc/tickets → pages/api/noc/tickets.ts
find pages/api/ -name "*.ts" | grep <keyword>

# Find the page component if error_url points to a UI page
# Example: error on /projects/123 → pages/projects/[id]/index.tsx
find pages/ -name "*.tsx" | grep <keyword>
```

**Step 2 — Reproduce the error:**

Use the `steps_to_reproduce` from the ticket. If it's a UI issue, use browser automation:

```
1. mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp  (get browser context)
2. mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate          (go to error_url)
3. mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page         (get page state)
4. mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer          (follow reproduction steps)
```

**Step 3 — Analyze the stack trace:**

If `stack_trace` is provided, trace it through the codebase:

```bash
# Search for the error message in code
rg "ErrorMessage" src/ pages/

# Check the specific file:line from stack trace
# Read the file at that location
```

**Step 4 — Check logs:**

```bash
# Dev server logs
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-dev.service --since "1 hour ago" | grep -i error

# Production logs
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-production.service --since "1 hour ago" | grep -i error

# Check for specific error patterns
sudo journalctl -u fibreflow-dev.service --since "1 hour ago" | grep "<ticket_keyword>"
```

**Step 5 — Database investigation:**

```sql
-- Check for data issues related to the ticket
-- Example: missing records, null values, constraint violations
SELECT * FROM <related_table> WHERE <condition> LIMIT 10;
```

### Phase 4: Fix Implementation

**Follow the PR workflow (MANDATORY):**

1. Create a feature branch: `fix/noc-<ticket_uid>-<short-description>`
2. Implement the fix
3. Run quality checks: `npm run lint && npm run type-check`
4. Run tests: `npm test`
5. Create PR via `/pr` skill
6. Update the ticket with PR link

**Update ticket status as you work:**

```sql
-- Mark ticket as in_progress when starting work
UPDATE maintenance_tickets SET status = 'in_progress' WHERE id = '<ticket_id>';

-- Update dev_ticket_details with branch/PR
UPDATE dev_ticket_details
SET github_branch = 'fix/noc-VF-XXXXXXXX-XXX-description',
    github_pr_url = 'https://github.com/VelocityFibre/FF_Next.js/pull/XXX',
    agent_status = 'running'
WHERE ticket_id = '<ticket_id>';
```

### Phase 5: Verification

DevOps tickets have 5 verification steps:

| Step | Name | Photo Required | Description |
|------|------|----------------|-------------|
| 1 | Issue Reproduction | Yes | Screenshot of the reproduced error |
| 2 | Root Cause Analysis | No | Document the root cause in notes |
| 3 | Fix Implementation | No | Link the PR, describe the fix |
| 4 | Testing & Verification | Yes | Screenshot of fix working in dev |
| 5 | Deployment | Yes | Screenshot of fix working in prod |

```bash
# Update verification step (example: step 2 - root cause)
curl -X PUT "http://localhost:3004/api/noc/tickets/<id>/verification/2" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "completed": true,
    "notes": "Root cause: missing null check in X component causing crash when Y is undefined"
  }'
```

#### MANDATORY: Upload Screenshots as Ticket Attachments

**Every screenshot taken during ticket work MUST be uploaded as a ticket attachment.**
Screenshots that only exist in `/tmp/` are lost when the session ends. The attachment API persists them permanently.

**How to upload a screenshot to a ticket:**

```bash
# 1. Take screenshot using browser tools (saves to /tmp/screenshot-*.png)
# 2. Upload to ticket attachments API:
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

const TICKET_ID = '<ticket-id>';
const FILE_PATH = '/tmp/screenshot.png';
const USER_ID = '<user-uid>';  // Use Hein's uid from auth context
const IS_EVIDENCE = 'true';    // true for verification step screenshots

const FormData = require('form-data');  // Built into Node 18+
const form = new FormData();
form.append('file', fs.createReadStream(FILE_PATH));
form.append('uploaded_by', USER_ID);
form.append('is_evidence', IS_EVIDENCE);

fetch('http://localhost:3004/api/noc/tickets/' + TICKET_ID + '/attachments', {
  method: 'POST',
  body: form,
}).then(r => r.json()).then(j => console.log(JSON.stringify(j, null, 2)));
"
```

**Or use the helper script:**

```bash
# Upload screenshot to ticket attachments
node scripts/noc-attach-screenshot.js <ticket-id> <file-path> [--evidence]
```

**When to upload screenshots:**

| Phase | Screenshot | `is_evidence` |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Step 1: Issue Reproduction | Screenshot showing the bug | `true` |
| Step 4: Testing & Verification | Screenshot showing fix works on dev | `true` |
| Step 5: Deployment | Screenshot showing fix works on prod | `true` |
| Diagnosis (optional) | Console errors, network tab, etc. | `false` |

**After fix is deployed and verified**, upload the "after" screenshot showing the issue is resolved:
1. Navigate to the affected page in the browser
2. Take a screenshot
3. Upload it with `is_evidence=true`
4. This provides proof-of-fix that persists on the ticket permanently

## Common Patterns (Known Issues)

### Pattern: API returns `data.data` (double-wrapped response)
**Symptom:** UI shows blank/undefined values
**Cause:** `apiResponse.success(res, { success: true, data: {...} })` double-wraps
**Fix:** Remove inner wrapper — just pass the raw data to `apiResponse.success(res, data)`
**Ref:** Memory `MEMORY.md` — "apiResponse.success() Double-Wrapping Anti-Pattern"

### Pattern: Conditional SQL fragment breaks Neon
**Symptom:** SQL syntax error, query returns unexpected results
**Cause:** `${cond ? sql\`AND x\` : sql\`\`}` — template literal fragments don't compose in Neon
**Fix:** Use explicit query branches (if/else with full queries)
**Ref:** CLAUDE.md — "NO Conditional SQL Fragments"

### Pattern: Dynamic route params `undefined`
**Symptom:** API returns 404 or "invalid UUID"
**Cause:** Nested dynamic routes fail on Vercel, or inconsistent param names
**Fix:** Flatten routes (`contractors-stages.ts` not `[id]/stages.ts`), use consistent `[projectId]`

### Pattern: Numeric values are strings from Neon
**Symptom:** Math operations return NaN or concatenate instead of add
**Cause:** Neon returns numeric columns as strings
**Fix:** Always `Number()` before arithmetic

### Pattern: Missing `credentials: 'include'` in fetch
**Symptom:** 401 Unauthorized on API calls
**Cause:** Auth cookie not sent with request
**Fix:** Add `credentials: 'include'` to all fetch calls

### Pattern: `console.log` in production code
**Symptom:** Lint error or log noise
**Fix:** Replace with `import { log } from '@/lib/logger'` — use `log.info()`, `log.error()`, etc.

### Pattern: File > 300 lines
**Symptom:** Quality violation
**Fix:** Extract components/utilities into separate files

Escalate (don't attempt to fix) when:

## Lessons Learned (Updated per ticket)

### 2026-03-13: VF-20260313-133 + VF-20260313-134
- **Schema column names differ from TypeScript types**: DB uses `type` not `ticket_type`, `status` not `ticket_status`. Always check actual schema with `\d maintenance_tickets` before querying.
- **psql connection**: Local psql defaults to port 5434 via socket. Use explicit: `PGPASSWORD=<pw> psql -h <host> -p 5432 -U neondb_owner -d neondb --set=sslmode=require`
- **z-index patterns**: ALL modals in codebase use `z-50` (not design tokens). Design system defines `--ff-z-modal-backdrop: 1040` and `--ff-z-modal: 1050` but they were never adopted. When fixing z-index, note this is a codebase-wide pattern, not a single-modal bug.
- **maintenance_notes schema**: Uses `created_by` (not `author_id`), has `is_resolution` boolean flag, `note_type` must be one of: internal, external, system.

# Create Pull Request

Create a pull request for the current branch following FF team standards.

## Pre-flight Checks

1. Verify clean working directory:
   ```bash
   git status
   ```

2. Get commit history for this branch:
   ```bash
   git log main..HEAD --oneline 2>/dev/null || git log develop..HEAD --oneline
   ```

3. See changed files:
   ```bash
   git diff main...HEAD --stat 2>/dev/null || git diff develop...HEAD --stat
   ```

## TDD Validation

Before creating PR, validate TDD compliance:

1. Check for test coverage:
   ```bash
   npm run test:coverage 2>/dev/null || npm test
   ```

2. Verify new code has tests:
   - For each new file in `src/modules/`, confirm test exists
   - Check `tests/specs/` for feature specification

## Analyze Changes

- Determine PR type: feat, fix, refactor, docs, test, chore
- Identify key changes and their purpose
- Note any breaking changes
- List what reviewers should focus on

## Create PR

```bash
gh pr create \
  --title "<type>: <description>" \

<1-3 bullet points explaining the change>

## Changes
- <list key files/components changed>

## Testing
- [ ] Unit tests pass (\`npm test\`)

- [ ] Manual testing completed

- [ ] Test spec exists: tests/specs/<feature>.spec.md
- [ ] Tests written before/during implementation
- [ ] Coverage maintained or improved

## Related
Closes #<issue-number> (if applicable)

---
Generated with Claude Code"
```

### 1. What the PR Does

Adds a new markdown reference document at `knowledge/fibreflow/pbi-visuals-reference.md` that defines Power BI-style visual standards for FibreFlow analytics dashboards. It covers:

- Colour palette (5 hex tokens with usage rules)
- KPI card structure, props, and per-report card definitions
- Table styling: currency formatting, conditional formatting, header/row styles
- Chart types by report
- WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility requirements
- File location reference for the analytics module

The PR states this was created because "Flow flagged that this file was missing when building PR #215 (PBI analytics tables)."

---

### 2. Code Quality

This is a documentation-only PR (no code changes), so traditional code quality concerns are minimal. The markdown itself is well-structured with clear tables, code examples, and consistent formatting.

---

### 3. Accuracy Concerns -- REQUEST CHANGES

**Major issue: The document references files and directories that do not exist.**

The "File Locations" section claims this structure exists:

```
src/modules/analytics/pbi/
    pbiTheme.ts
    KpiCard.tsx
```

Neither `src/modules/analytics/pbi/` nor any files within it exist in the codebase. The document repeatedly references `pbiTheme.ts` (for colour tokens, `formatCurrency()`, `getGPColor()`) and `KpiCard.tsx` as if they are established, importable modules. They are not.

The table files (`CashflowTable.tsx`, `ProjectRevenueTable.tsx`, etc.) under `src/modules/analytics/reports/tables/` **do** exist, so that part is accurate.

This is a significant problem for a document described as "the source of truth." Anyone reading it will expect to import from `@/modules/analytics/pbi/pbiTheme` and find `KpiCard.tsx` there, then waste time when those files are missing.

---

### 4. Additional Concerns

1. **Location choice:** This is the first file under `knowledge/fibreflow/`. The project already has established documentation locations: `.claude/modules/`, `.claude/knowledge-base/`, and `docs/`. Adding a new top-level `knowledge/` directory creates a fourth documentation location. This should either go into `.claude/knowledge-base/` (which is purpose-built for this) or `docs/`.

2. **Branch naming:** The branch is `elon/pbi-visuals-reference` -- the `elon/` prefix is unusual for this project's conventions (`feature/`, `fix/`, `docs/` are the expected patterns per CLAUDE.md).

3. **Aspirational vs. actual:** The document reads like a specification for code that does not yet exist (the `pbi/` subdirectory with theme and KPI card components). If that is the intent, it should be clearly marked as a spec/proposal rather than presented as a reference to existing code. Otherwise it violates the NLNH protocol -- it presents non-existent files as existing.

4. **CSS variable references are unverified:** The document references `--ff-bg-tertiary`, `--ff-bg-secondary`, and `--ff-bg-hover` CSS variables. These should be verified to exist in the theme.

---

### 5. Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The document is well-written and the content would be valuable, but it needs fixes before merging:

- **Must fix:** Either create the referenced `pbi/pbiTheme.ts` and `pbi/KpiCard.tsx` files, or clearly mark those sections as "to be implemented" rather than presenting them as existing code.

## YouTube Transcript

Get subtitles/transcript from a YouTube video. Try auto-generated captions first, fall back to whisper.

```bash
# Step 1: List available subtitles
yt-dlp --list-subs "URL" 2>&1 | head -20

# Step 2: Download subtitles (prefer manual, fall back to auto-generated)
yt-dlp --write-sub --write-auto-sub --sub-lang en --sub-format vtt \
  --skip-download -o "/tmp/transcript" "URL"

# Step 3: Clean VTT to plain text (removes timestamps, deduplicates)
python3 << 'PYEOF'
import re, sys

def clean_vtt(path):
    with open(path) as f:
        text = f.read()
    # Remove VTT header and timestamps
    lines = text.split('\n')
    seen, result = set(), []
    for line in lines:
```

```bash
# Browser Automation Skill

Automate Chrome browser interactions using two MCP tool sets.

## Tool Sets

| MCP | Best For | Prefix |
|-----|----------|--------|
| **claude-in-chrome** | Page reading, navigation, form filling, screenshots, GIFs | `mcp__claude-in-chrome__` |
| **chrome-devtools** | Low-level DOM, network inspection, performance, JS execution | `mcp__chrome-devtools__` |

---

## Quick Start (EVERY session)

**Always start with tab context:**
```
mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
```
This returns current tabs. Use an existing tab or create a new one.

---

## Task Router

| Intent | Tools to Use |
|--------|-------------|
| Open a URL | [Navigate](#navigate) |
| Read page content | [Read Page](#read-page) |
| Click / interact | [Click & Type](#click--type) |
| Fill a form | [Form Fill](#form-fill) |
| Take screenshot | [Screenshot](#screenshot) |
| Record multi-step flow | [GIF Recording](#gif-recording) |
| Run JavaScript | [JavaScript](#javascript) |
| Check network requests | [Network](#network) |
| Read console logs | [Console](#console) |

---

## Navigate

```
# Claude-in-Chrome (preferred)
mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate → url: "https://example.com"

# DevTools (alternative)
mcp__chrome-devtools__navigate_page → url: "https://example.com"

# Create new tab first if needed
mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp → url: "https://example.com"
```

---

## Read Page

```
# Accessibility tree (structured, best for understanding layout)
mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page → format: "accessibility"

# Full text content
mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text

# Take snapshot (DevTools)
mcp__chrome-devtools__take_snapshot
```

---

## Click & Type

```
# Click by description (Claude-in-Chrome finds the element)
mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer → action: "click", description: "Submit button"

# Click by coordinates
mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer → action: "click", x: 500, y: 300

# Type text

# DevTools click (by CSS selector)

# DevTools type

# Deployment Workflow — Two Environments (2026-03-11)

## RULE: Dev-only during business hours

| Time | Dev | Production |
|------|-----|------------|
| 08:00-17:00 SAST Mon-Fri | Allowed | BLOCKED |
| After hours + weekends | Allowed | Promote from dev |
| Emergency (any time) | Allowed | --force required |

> **Staging retired 2026-03-11.** `vf.fibreflow.app` redirects to `app.fibreflow.app`. Standalone services (wa-proxy :8092, pdf-tools :3007) still route through the old vf.fibreflow.app nginx block.

## Environments

| Env | URL | Port | Service | Dir |
|-----|-----|------|---------|-----|
| Dev | dev.fibreflow.app | 3005 | `fibreflow-dev.service` | `/home/velo/fibreflow-dev/` |
| Production | app.fibreflow.app | 3000 | `fibreflow-production.service` | `/home/velo/fibreflow-production/` |
| Local | localhost:3004 | 3004 | manual | working copy |

## Primary: deploy-local.sh (one command, handles everything)

```bash
bash scripts/deploy-local.sh dev              # Deploy to dev (always)
bash scripts/deploy-local.sh production       # After hours only
bash scripts/deploy-local.sh status           # Show all environments
bash scripts/deploy-local.sh production --force  # Emergency override
```

**What it handles automatically:**
- Ownership fix (`sudo chown -R velo:velo`) — prevents EACCES from mixed hein/velo/root builds
- Stops service before build (prevents crash-loop interference)
- Cleans stale `.next` artifacts (backs up to `.next-backup-TIMESTAMP`)
- Build retry up to 3 attempts (Next.js 14 race condition on rename/unlink is transient)
- Validates BUILD_ID after build
- Starts service + HTTP health check on /sign-in
- Keeps last 3 `.next-backup-*` builds for rollback

## Other Scripts

- `scripts/deploy-gate.sh` — Auto-redirects to `deploy-local.sh` on Velocity (hostname detection). Falls back to SSH for remote use.
- `scripts/promote.sh` — Promotion pipeline: `dev → production` (exact commit)

## /deploy Skill

- `/deploy` or `/deploy dev` — deploy to dev (always)
- `/deploy production` — after hours only
- `/deploy production --force` — emergency override
- `/deploy status` — show all environments

## Maintenance Page

Nginx serves `/var/www/html/maintenance.html` on 502/503 during restarts:
- Branded "Upgrading FibreFlow" page with spinner
- Auto-refreshes every 8 seconds
- Returns 200 status (bypasses Cloudflare's error page interception)
- Source: `deployment/maintenance.html` in repo

## Git Hooks

**Pre-commit** (`.git/hooks/pre-commit`):
- Auto-allows non-code files on master: `.claude/`, `.github/`, `docs/`, `scripts/`, `*.md`
- Still blocks code changes (`.ts`, `.tsx`, etc.) on master — forces feature branch workflow
- Override: `ALLOW_MASTER_COMMIT=1 git commit -m "..."`

**Pre-push** (`.git/hooks/pre-push`):
- GUARD 1: Allows Claude Code sessions (checks `CLAUDECODE=1` env var)
- GUARD 2: Auth isolation scan (scans for hardcoded userId patterns)
- Override: `ALLOW_MASTER_PUSH=1 git push`

## Sudoers

**hein's sudo password**: `0203`

| File | Rule |
|------|------|
| `/etc/sudoers.d/hein-nopasswd` | `hein ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL` |
| `/etc/sudoers.d/fibreflow-deploy` | `hein ALL=(velo) NOPASSWD: ALL` + service restarts |

## File Ownership Fix

**Root cause**: Three users create files in deploy dirs — velo (services), hein (manual git/npm), root (previous sudo builds).

**Fix**: `/usr/local/bin/fibreflow-fix-next` — run before builds if ownership breaks:
```bash
sudo /usr/local/bin/fibreflow-fix-next /home/velo/fibreflow-dev
sudo /usr/local/bin/fibreflow-fix-next /home/velo/fibreflow-production
```

## Key Decisions
- Staging removed — added complexity with zero value (all envs share same DB, no separate QA team)
- Promotions deploy the EXACT commit from dev (not latest master)
- Emergency overrides require typing "EMERGENCY" to confirm
- All environments share production DB — schema changes affect everyone immediately

# Fleet Check-In Improvements (2026-02-06)

## Low VLM Confidence Flag
**Problem**: Check-ins with 0% VLM confidence (photos of feet, wrong subjects) showed "All Passed".
**Solution**: Added `hasLowVlmConfidence` flag — if any VLM photo <50% confidence, sets `hasMinorIssues = true`.

**Files**: `fleet/types/check-in.types.ts`, `fleet/check-in/hooks/useCheckIn.ts`, `fleet/services/checkInService.ts`

## Merged Audit into History Page
Consolidated `/fleet/check-in/audit` and `/fleet/check-in/history` into single Check-Ins page.
- Shows VLM results, odometer discrepancies, approval status
- Admin can approve/reject/delete; non-admins see own check-ins only

**Files**: `pages/fleet/check-in/history.tsx` (rewritten), `audit.tsx` (deleted), `fleet.config.ts` (nav updated)

## Admin Delete — Cascade Order
```
DELETE /api/fleet/check-in/records/[recordId]  (admin/super_admin only)
1. fleet_photo_vlm_results (by photo_id)
2. fleet_check_photos
3. fleet_check_responses
4. fleet_odometer_history
5. fleet_fuel_history
6. fleet_check_records
```

## Role Check Pattern
```typescript
const user = (req as unknown as { user?: { role?: string } }).user;
if (!user || (user.role !== 'admin' && user.role !== 'super_admin')) {
  return apiResponse.error(res, ErrorCode.FORBIDDEN, 'Only admins can delete');
}
```

## Non-Admin Access Control
```typescript
const isAdmin = user?.role === 'admin' || user?.role === 'super_admin';
if (!isAdmin && user?.id) {
  filters.push(`cr.driver_id = $${paramIndex++}`);
  params.push(user.id);
}
```

## Weekly vs Daily Check-Ins
| Feature | Daily | Weekly |
|---------|-------|--------|
| Required Photos | 2 (dashboard, fuel) | 4 (front, rear, dashboard, fuel) |
| Optional Photos | 0 | 3 (under vehicle, license disk, damage) |
| VLM Processing | Odometer, fuel gauge | License plate (x2), odometer, fuel gauge |
| Checklist Items | 2 items | 16 items across 3 categories |

**DB Templates**: daily="Daily Quick Check" (2 items), weekly="Weekly Pre-Trip Inspection" (16 items)
